body.en: In a collector modulator, a class C RF amplifier is driven by the carrier at its base, and the audio signal is connected in series with the collector supply (through a modulation transformer). The effective collector voltage becomes $V_{CC} + v_m$, so the amplitude of the RF output in the tuned collector circuit varies with the audio. Modulation at the final power stage is called high-level modulation; modulation at a low-power stage (for example a base modulator) is low-level modulation.

points.en: Carrier at the base, audio in series with VCC
Tuned LC tank at the collector, resonant at fc

narration.en: In a collector modulator the audio adds to the collector supply of a class C RF amplifier, so the RF output amplitude follows the audio.
narration.kn: ಕಲೆಕ್ಟರ್ ಮಾಡ್ಯುಲೇಟರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಧ್ವನಿ ಸಂಕೇತವು ಕ್ಲಾಸ್ C RF ಆಂಪ್ಲಿಫೈಯರ್‌ನ ಕಲೆಕ್ಟರ್ ಪೂರೈಕೆಗೆ ಸೇರುತ್ತದೆ, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ RF ಔಟ್‌ಪುಟ್ ವೈಶಾಲ್ಯ ಧ್ವನಿಯನ್ನು ಅನುಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: Making and detecting AM

say.en: In a collector modulator, a class C amplifier is driven by the carrier, and its tuned tank sends the RF to the aerial.
The audio is added in series with the collector supply. So the supply becomes VCC plus the message, and the RF output follows it.
Modulating at the final power stage is high-level modulation; at an early, weak stage it is low-level modulation.
To detect AM, a diode lets through only the positive peaks. The capacitor charges to each peak and leaks slowly through R.
So the voltage across RC traces the envelope: the original message comes back.
RC must be long compared with a carrier cycle but short compared with a message cycle. Too small leaves ripple; too large clips.

narration.en: The diode lets the capacitor charge to each carrier peak; between peaks it discharges through R. With RC much longer than the carrier period (0.05 ms) but shorter than the message allows, the output follows the envelope. Too small an RC leaves carrier ripple; too large and the output cannot fall fast enough (diagonal clipping).
narration.kn: ಡಯೋಡ್ ಧಾರಕವನ್ನು ಪ್ರತಿ ವಾಹಕ ಶಿಖರಕ್ಕೆ ಆವೇಶಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ನಡುವೆ R ಮೂಲಕ ವಿಸರ್ಜಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಸರಿಯಾದ RC ಯಲ್ಲಿ ನಿರ್ಗಮ ಆವರಣವನ್ನು ಅನುಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ತುಂಬಾ ಸಣ್ಣ RC ಏರಿಳಿತ, ತುಂಬಾ ದೊಡ್ಡ RC ಕರ್ಣ ಕ್ಲಿಪ್ಪಿಂಗ್.

body.en: Demodulation (detection) recovers the message from the modulated wave. In the diode detector the diode conducts only on positive half cycles; the capacitor charges to each RF peak and discharges slowly through R between peaks, so the voltage across RC follows the envelope. A coupling capacitor then removes the DC. The time constant must satisfy $1/f_c \ll RC \ll 1/f_m$: too small leaves RF ripple, too large causes diagonal clipping.

points.en: Diode rectifies, RC filters the carrier

narration.en: In the diode detector the capacitor charges to each peak and discharges slowly through R, so the output follows the envelope. RC must be much more than one carrier period but much less than one message period.
narration.kn: ಡಯೋಡ್ ಡಿಟೆಕ್ಟರ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಪಾಸಿಟರ್ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಶಿಖರಕ್ಕೆ ಚಾರ್ಜ್ ಆಗಿ R ಮೂಲಕ ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಡಿಸ್ಚಾರ್ಜ್ ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಔಟ್‌ಪುಟ್ ಎನ್ವಲಪ್ ಅನ್ನು ಅನುಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. 1/fc ≪ RC ≪ 1/fm.

narration.en: The detector capacitor charges quickly through the diode and discharges through R. Measure the RC time constant here and imagine how fast it lets the output fall.

caption.en: Choose R and C of the envelope detector and the two frequencies. Keep RC·fc much bigger than 1 and RC·fm much smaller than 1.

tryThis.en: With 10 kΩ and 2 nF, RC = 20 µs: 20 carrier cycles but only a tenth of a message cycle. Good.
Raise C to 20 nF: RC·fm reaches 1, and the output would clip on falling parts of the envelope.

With 10 kΩ and 2 nF, RC = 20 µs: 20 carrier cycles but only a tenth of a message cycle. Good. Raise C to 20 nF: RC·fm reaches 1, and the output would clip on falling parts of the envelope.

problem.en: An envelope detector receives an AM wave with fc = 455 kHz and highest audio fm = 5 kHz. The load is R = 10 kΩ. Choose a suitable C.

steps.en: Choose RC between them, e.g. about the geometric mean √(2.2 × 200) ≈ 21 µs; take RC = 20 µs.

answer.en: C ≈ 2 nF (RC ≈ 20 µs, between 2.2 µs and 200 µs)
